DEEPENING

STATUTES

SESSIONS – STUDY GUIDE

1992

PRESENTATION

This guide is meant to help in reading and deepening the “Statutes” of the Movement of Hope.

The booklet consists of 25 sessions, prepared in the form of a liturgical celebration for the weekly meetings.

The themes of each session are linked to the topics of the Statutes themselves; this is why the Scripture readings were chosen as they were.

The questions in each session – after the reading of the Word – are aimed at:

  • helping each one become aware of their own call in the Church and in the Movement;
  • interiorizing the Word that has been proclaimed;
  • helping to live a stronger experience of community prayer;
  • deepening the charism and the spirituality through the articles of the Statutes and the experience of Mother Rosa;
  • checking one’s own sense of belonging to the Movement;
  • helping the group grow in communication and in communion;

Each session may be completed in one or more meetings, and can offer ideas for prayer, reflection and personal deepening during the week as well.

The introduction to each celebration will be suitably prepared by the Leader (assisted, of course, by the Sister), who may also use – for a greater personal enrichment of the contents – the guides given in previous years, as well as the letters (booklets) of Mother Virginia, the writings of Mother Rosa, or other documents and sources of the spirituality.

We hope that these simple directions may help you enter into the spirit of the guide and use it effectively.

The Central Team
of the Movement of Hope

OUTLINE – GUIDE

for the celebrations

  • Opening hymn
  • Introduction, by the Leader (or the Sister), of the theme of the meeting, with essential points that prepare for listening and foster – in an atmosphere of prayer – a deepening of the contents proposed in each session.
  • Reading of one or more articles of the Statutes, as indicated in the session.
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours, depending on the time of day when the meeting takes place).
  • Substitute Scripture reading (indicated in each session).
  • Pause for silence and personal reflection in the light of the questions provided.
  • Sharing of one’s own experience.
  • Singing of the Magnificat (with a suitable introduction) or another hymn.
  • Prayer of the Our Father, concluding prayer, suitable hymn.

SESSION 1

THE CALL IN THE MOVEMENT

(Vocation to the spirituality of the Movement)

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 2 and 3
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Reading: Jn 1:35–51 (in place of the short reading)
  • After a pause for silence, to interiorize the texts we have heard, let yourselves be addressed by the following questions:
    • What does it mean for you to be called to collaborate in the Church for the spread of the Kingdom, with the attitude of poverty of heart and dedication that was typical of St Anne?
    • Do you also feel that you are an object of predilection, called and sent to carry out – even in your own small way – a mission?
    • What did it involve for Mother Rosa to collaborate in the Church for the spread of the Kingdom and to receive the charism?
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 2

ST ANNE

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes art. 4
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Reading: 1 Sm 1 (in place of the short reading)
  • Silence, to interiorize the texts we have heard
  • Points for personal reflection and the sharing that follows:
    • What biblical figures does Hannah, the mother of Samuel, bring to your mind? And what link can you establish between this mother and St Anne?
    • In the painful moments that you have lived or are living now, do you place your total trust in God, or are you inclined to be discouraged, to murmur, to rebel when you are visited by trial or humiliation?
    • What was Mother Rosa’s experience in this regard? Recall some particular episodes.
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father and concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 3

SIGN OF HOPE

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 5 and 6
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Reading: Rom 5:1–11
  • Silence for reflection and interiorization
  • Suggestions for deepening the theme:
    • God is faithful to His promises, always shows mercy, and His hope does not disappoint;
    • In what sense did the Poor of Yahweh live these truths?
    • What experience have you had in your life of God’s faithfulness? Are you aware that God intervenes also in your personal and family history?
    • Do you live this with gratitude, with the attitude proper to the poor?
    • Were there particular interventions of God in the life of Mother Rosa? What was her attitude toward God?
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 4

MARY

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 7 and 8
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Lk 1:26–38
  • Pause for silence and personal reflection on the readings we have heard, helped by the questions:
    • Why does the Remnant of Israel see in Mary the first response of God to the hope of the Poor? Why the choice of Mary?
    • Mary made herself fully available to God and to the fulfillment of His promises.
    • Mother Rosa was open and available to the Lord – In what way was she a sign of hope for the people of her time? And is she still so for us today?
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 5

THE SERVANT OF YAHWEH

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes art. 9
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Isaiah 53
  • Pause for silence and reflection
  • Questions for personal and group deepening:
    • Outline the features and all the characteristics of the Servant of Yahweh
    • What does this figure say to you? Are you willing to share (in your family, at work…) the mission of Jesus the Servant, without splendor, without success, with gentleness…?
    • Does it seem possible to you today to live these characteristics?
    • What place did the Crucified One = the Suffering Servant occupy in the life of Mother Rosa?
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 6

THE MISSION OF THE SERVANT

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 10–12
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Is 42:1–9
  • Silence for meditation on the passages we have heard
  • Questions for reflection:
    • To whom is the mission of the Servant of Yahweh directed?
    • And how does he carry it out?
    • Are you willing to share with the poor your time, your energies, your abilities, with the attitudes proper to the Servant, in the spirit of the Beatitudes?
    • Does Mother Rosa, as Foundress, follow in her mission the attitudes of the servant?
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 7

PURPOSE AND SPIRITUALITY OF THE MOVEMENT

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 14–16
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Reading: Lk 9:57–62
  • Pause for silence
  • For interiorizing and sharing, let yourselves be guided by the following questions:
    • Christ became poor in order to make you rich. Are you aware of this gift, of being called to follow Jesus and to persevere on the way with Him, deepening your baptismal consecration?
    • Have you ever thought that you too are on the way to holiness with the brothers and sisters of the Movement, and that the holiness of others also depends on you and on your commitment to Christ?
    • Holiness was the constant longing of Mother Rosa’s life; for it she gave her whole self, to it she urged on…
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 8

IN THE CLIMATE OF COMMUNION

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes art. 17
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Acts 2:42–48
  • Pause for silence for meditation
  • Questions for reflection:
    • What were the fundamental characteristics of the first Christian communities? On what values was their life based?
    • Do you feel the need for a spiritual journey made together with the brothers and sisters of the Movement, even with the inevitable difficulties, uncertainties, crises…, or do you think you can manage on your own?
    • On what foundations and values did Mother Rosa build her communities, and how did she form the persons entrusted to her? What would she say today to our groups to help them grow in fraternal communion?
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 9

WITH THE ATTITUDE OF THE POOR, ANIMATED BY FAITH

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 18–19
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Gen 15
  • Pause for silence
  • Guiding questions for reflection:
    • Are you willing to guard the treasure of faith, defending it from worldly compromises and striving to remain, like Abraham, like Mary… a poor pilgrim waiting for God to bring His promises to fulfillment?
    • Do you believe that your baptism is a gift that God has given you in the Church to lead you to the riches of that inheritance that will truly make you… “a child of God”?
    • Mother Rosa, like Abraham, like Mary…, believed in God’s promises, trusted in Him, and was able to perceive His presence in all the events of her life. Can you recall some particular episode? What lessons for your life today?
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 10

… FROM HOPE…

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 20–23
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Reading: Rom 4:16–25
  • Meditative silence
  • For personal reflection:
    • In what hope does the person of today place his or her security? And what does it mean for you “to hope against hope”?
    • As a member of the Movement, do you walk toward Christ, do you seek the kingdom of God and His righteousness, do you abandon yourself to Him… do you accept to take part in the paschal mystery of Christ? Is the Risen Christ your hope?
    • In what way did Mother Rosa take part in the paschal mystery of Christ?
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 11

… AND FROM CHARITY

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 24–28…
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Reading: Jn 15:10–25
  • Pause for silence and reflection, helped by the following questions:
    • To belong to the Church also means to be part of a “body” in which one experiences the knowledge of God, His intimacy and the gift of full joy; are you aware of this?
    • Do you desire Christ to reveal His friendship to you? But how willing are you to obey Him, to bear with Him the contempt and the hatred of the world?
    • What attitudes must you cultivate in order to live in the love of God and of neighbor?
    • By what signs do you recognize that you are reaching toward this?
    • Mother Rosa wanted love for God and mutual love to show itself in the concrete attitudes of daily life: “aim at one center, who is God. True charity and love toward one another must be so sincere that the good one wants for oneself must be wanted for others also… love one another, and let charity be what accompanies you in all your actions…”

      • Let us allow ourselves to be addressed.

  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 12

THEY GROW IN THE VIRTUES PECULIAR TO SIMPLICITY…

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 29–30
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Num 12
  • Silence, to interiorize the texts we have heard
  • Questions for personal and group reflection:
    • The sins of gossip, jealousy, envy, quarrels, disputes… are against simplicity. Are you aware that if the Church, the Parish, the group, your family…, do not grow – and therefore do not move forward – it is often, sadly, because of this “leprosy”?
    • What does it mean for you today to live in sincerity and uprightness: with God, with yourself, with your family, in your work environment, in the Movement? etc.
    • Can you say, in all sincerity, that in everything you do you look to what pleases God most? And that you fear, above all, His judgment?
    • Mother Rosa wants to form us in this virtue that was so dear to her heart. Let us listen and make her teaching our own: “let truth always be upon our lips, and simplicity in our heart…] let truth be your treasure always…! sincerity, charity) the love of God is the only thing we need; all the rest is a fine nothing or less than Nothing… Act with an upright purpose, always in the presence of God, with truth in your heart and on your lips…”
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 13

… AND PRUDENCE

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 31 and 32
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Gen 33
  • Silence and personal reflection on the guiding questions:
    • Jacob is famous for his cunning and… prudently, though reconciled, he will keep Esau at a distance from himself.

      • Are you equally prudent in preserving the richness of your election as a “child of God,” not “lingering” on the path of sinners (Psalm 1)? What does the world understand today by “prudence”?

    • In your practical daily life, in the choices you make, in the important decisions… do you let yourself be guided by prudence according to the Spirit, putting first what is best according to the will of God?
    • Do you seek, in listening to the Word and in prayer, the light needed for the way to follow?
    • Have you experienced in your life what Mother Rosa says: “only Jesus is our sure pledge, all the rest is deceptive and fleeting. People are weathervanes in the wind, bending where it blows hardest.” “… prudence… leads you to acquire and increase the only wealth, that is, the love of God.”
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 14

OF HUMILITY…

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 33–36
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Phil 2:3–11
  • Pause for silence for interiorizing the texts we have heard
  • For personal reflection and sharing, let the word you have heard penetrate you in the light of the teaching of Jesus: “learn from me, for I am meek and humble of heart”:
    • This virtue was an essential characteristic of the poor of Yahweh (and therefore of St Anne, of Mary…) and so also of the Movement. Why?
    • Does the word we have heard speak to me?
    • What must I change in my life in order to live this virtue?
    • Do I know how to recognize the gifts of God in myself and in others, do I know how to place them willingly and simply at the service of the brothers and sisters, have I ever tasted the joy of being in the last place, do I let myself be attracted by what is humble?
    • Do you feel that it is possible to live today, personally and as a group, what Mother Rosa tells us: “Keep yourselves humble, because this is the only way not to fall and to become saints”
      • “Be humble like the little poor ones, always think that you are the last and the most wretched of all the creatures who give their service to the Church and have the good fortune to be part of it.”
    • What does all this concretely involve?
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 15

… AND MEEKNESS…

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 37–38
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Lk 10:25–37
  • Pause for silence for reflection
  • Questions for interiorizing, deepening and personal discussion:
    • What does it mean for you that, in love toward neighbor, it is necessary to clothe ourselves with feelings of mercy, kindness, “com-passion”… the very ones with which you yourself are clothed each day by the love of God?
    • Are you able to get involved with the weaknesses, the faults and the resistance of your brothers and sisters, not being scandalized, not judging them, but accepting them patiently, and persevering with them on the path that God has given you – with this Movement – asking Him for yourself and for them conversion of heart, forgiveness and salvation?
    • For growth in the virtue of meekness, let yourself be helped by some experience of Mother Rosa and by her teaching: “do everything calmly… I recommend meekness to you.”
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 16

… IN TIRELESS DEDICATION LIKE THE CHURCH, BRIDE AND MOTHER

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes arts. 39–40
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Esther 4:1–17
  • Pause for personal reflection and sharing in the group
  • Suggestions for interiorizing the texts proclaimed:
    • Does the figure of Esther remind you of any other significant biblical person?
    • Is there in you that motherly desire to offer yourself, to risk your life for the salvation of your brothers and sisters?
    • Have you ever thought that God expresses in you His fatherly and motherly love, making you fruitful and welcoming?
    • On what occasion did the Lord give you the grace of experiencing this?

      • If you wish, you may share your experience.

    • We know well the awareness that Mother Rosa had of the gift of motherhood and how she lived it in the Church, first as a lay woman and then as a Foundress.

      • Let us grasp it also through these expressions of hers:

      • “I feel an obligation of conscience that urges me on: humanity is falling back…!”
      • “If nothing has been able to stop my steps for your good and for the greater glory of God, I assure you that, until my last breath, I will always be the same and will not fail to come to your aid in any need of yours”
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 17

THE MEMBERS OF THE MOVEMENT LIVE IN CHARITY IN THE SPIRIT OF THE “POOR”

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes art. 41
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Lk 18:1–8
  • Pause for silence for reflection
  • Questions for interiorizing, deepening and personal discussion:
    • What value and how much room does the person of today give to prayer? What place does it have in your day and in your life?
    • Do you believe in the effectiveness of persevering prayer, even in the awareness of your own inconstancy and wretchedness? Do you know how to wait in it like the Poor of Yahweh, keeping watch, without growing weary, without losing heart, trusting that God will hear you?
    • Mother Rosa teaches us how to persevere in prayer:
      • “I pray every day and at every moment”
      • “do not forget to stay always in the presence of God the Father Remember the instructions that this wretched woman gave you Ah, how happy to be united with the good God”
      • “do not doubt my remembrance of you, because I assure you that you hold the greatest place in it, and I always present your soul to God that He may adorn it with His grace And so great is the trust I have in this most tender Father that my offering will be accepted by Him and everything will be poured into it…”
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 18

THEY NOURISH PRAYER

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes art. 42
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or Lauds, or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Mt 6:5–15
  • Silence for reflection and interiorization
  • Suggestions for deepening the theme, in the light of the following questions:
    • The purpose of every life is the knowledge of God, the coming of His Kingdom and the eternal possession of His happiness. On this reality… the people of Israel – the Poor of Yahweh above all – based their hope. Is it also the fundamental purpose of your life?
    • Are you called to discover, you too, day by day, the importance of personal dialogue with God in order to enter into His saving Will, to open yourself more and more to the action of His Spirit and to be an instrument of His mercy. What are you doing to carry out and nourish this important dimension of your life? Is it easy for you to be silent, to listen, … to feed on the Word and on the Eucharist?
    • Mother Rosa lived prayer intensely as an immediate, tender, trusting and spousal relationship with God:
      • “Oh, sweetness beyond compare! oh, blessed is the one who comes to taste and possess this divine essence…Go, go and suck the honey of sweetness) It is its very essence, So run to its fountain and drink, drink deeply!…”
      • “Woe to the creature who has made herself deaf to the inspirations that God, in His mercy, gives her”
      • “Let us pray with fervor, so that our prayers may reach the loving heart of Jesus, there where the source of every spiritual and temporal wealth is found”
    • Go back and reflect personally on these expressions and try to grasp the meaning they have for you, as an heir of her same call, in the Movement.
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 19

GATHERED BY THE WORD

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes art. 43
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Reading: Rom 10:11–17
  • Pause for silence and questions for reflection:
    • Can you say that you believe in God, that you know Him, that you love Him, that you entrust yourself to Him?
    • What makes you say so? Do you desire that the whole “mystery” of salvation, contained in the treasures of the Scriptures, be made known to you?

      • Ask for it humbly in prayer!

    • How can you know this “mystery”: the divine plan revealed to the Apostles by Jesus, if you do not seriously desire the times of preparation and initiation that the Church wants to put at your disposal, through the Movement, for your growth?

      • Do you take part in these moments with joy and willingness?

    • Mother Rosa experienced, like all the great apostles, the tension between the need to seek divine intimacy in silence… and, on the other hand, the urge to bring to others the “Good” known and received, spreading truth and love, that is, drawing people closer to God:
      • “My Love! How! I feel myself burning with desire to make you known and loved by all! may your name be blessed by every tongue. My God! Oh, that I could make everyone feel what I feel”
      • “My Good, how can I make you known to the whole world? Oh! How many there are who do not know you! and those who have known you flee from you, never having seen you. I would like to run everywhere and cry out loudly that everyone would come to love you”
    • What do these strong and meaningful expressions stir up in you?
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 20

IN A NEED FOR CONVERSION

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes art. 44
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Reading: Col 3:1–13
  • Questions for reflection:
    • You are on the way: much of you is still “earth” and darkness – You have not entirely put on Christ. How willing are you to fight against your passions?
    • How many evil desires and insatiable greed still stir your heart, not too open to the “things that are above”?
    • Are you willing to forgive, to bear patiently with the faults of the brothers and sisters of the group, of the Parish, of other movements? How do you live your state of life and the difficulties you meet?
    • Do you carry with love the weight of faithfulness to your duty in the reality of daily life?
    • Mother Rosa lived conversion as a debt of love to be paid at any cost, for herself and for others:
      • “Always clinging to my Good, I went on repeating: Oh! my sins deserve worse, and hell itself…”
      • “… I hope everything from your infinite mercy, which is such in me that I feel that my wretchedness, everything I have committed and commit of imperfection will be forgiven by your infinite mercy) and You, my love, will embrace me without merit – This I hope, but your Passion assures me of everything,”
      • “The sorrows of my family were beyond compare, I poured everything into the heart of my dear Crucified One, for Him alone, I went on telling myself, all my suffering is little, because I had committed many sins…”
      • “Oh! My Love, use once more this wretched instrument of yours to revive the faith and the conversion of sinners”
    • Comparing myself with the experience of Mother Rosa, do I feel that I must begin or intensify my journey of perfection? How? Do I let myself be personally addressed?
  • Sharing
  • Singing of the Magnificat (or another hymn)
  • Intercessions (from the Breviary, and spontaneous)
  • Our Father
  • Concluding prayer
  • Hymn (suited to the celebration)

SESSION 21

THEY RECEIVE THE GRACE OF FORGIVENESS

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes art. 45
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Substitute reading: Jas 4:1, 12–16; 5:19–20
  • Pause for silence:
  • Questions for reflection
    • The cause of all the evils that afflict us is the envy of the devil, who has divided us from God, from others, from ourselves.
    • Are you convinced that for a serious return to God it is necessary to confess our pride, our anger, our unrestrained love of money, and to call on the help of Jesus, the “poor and meek lamb,” who alone has the power to restore us to His friendship and to put us back together in peace?
    • How sincere in you is the sorrow for your life so often badly spent, seeking and asking only for what is earthly, fleeting, vain, and without much interest or concern for what is eternal and true?
    • Do you feel the need to “enrich” your life for God? Do you willingly approach the Sacrament of Penance?
    • Mother Rosa, strongly experiencing God’s forgiveness and the need to be continually forgiven, expressed this gratitude of hers throughout her life, in a thousand ways:
      • “I only look at the grace that God gives me so abundantly that, while I receive such sad affronts and wicked insults, I feel not the slightest resentment toward the one who offends me, indeed I feel such an impulse that I desire nothing else than to be able to do them good”
      • And again: “Let us bless the hand of the Almighty, who gently strikes us and in His charity makes us pay our debts in this foreign passage of short duration…”
    • Finally, to obtain the forgiveness of others:
      • “I would always have striven to lift up and seek the conversion of the poor sinner, your love for ungrateful man, your suffering for his salvation so urges me to make vows and firm promises to give myself entirely for the Poor Sinner… and if I succeed in saving someone I will bring them to your feet My Love”
    • With what attitudes do you live the grace of God’s “forgiveness”? Do you strive so that others too may experience the joy of reconciliation with God and with their brothers and sisters?

SESSION 22

STRENGTHENED BY THE EUCHARISTIC MYSTERY

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes art. 46
  • Brief pause for silence
  • Celebration of Vespers (or another hour of the Liturgy of the Hours)
  • Reading: Lk 22:1–20
  • Silence for meditation on the passages we have heard
  • Questions for reflection:
    • Do you realize that your whole life, even with its dark moments, is lit up and wrapped in this burning love of Jesus, who from eternity foresaw and wanted this encounter of love with you, made you know it in this sacrament given to the apostles and still preserved for you today by the faithfulness of the Spirit of the Lord to His Church?
    • What does it mean for you to “keep the Passover” with Jesus, to walk as He did toward the Father, to live the Exodus today?
    • Is the Eucharist at the center of your life?
    • From her youth Mother Rosa was drawn to the Eucharistic mystery, which little by little became something vital, both as nourishment of the Spirit in the Sacrament, and as a bond of offering in the sacrifice, and as an attraction of love in the Tabernacle:
      • “You will have a special devotion to Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament…”
      • “Fill me, for pity’s sake, with Your Love! Oh! why do I not remain forever before your tabernacle, where You, my Beloved, are shut in? What are five, six hours a day? Nothing! Let me stay close to you…”
      • “Before Jesus time has no time”
      • “If people knew you…, they would come to the foot of your altar to enjoy your delights”
      • “… make sure that during the day you honor Him frequently with mental visits or spiritual communions”
    • Let yourself be addressed by her example!

IN COMMUNION WITH THE HOLY MOTHER

    • “… in me all the justice and all the holiness of the ancient law found, as it were, their fulfillment; in me rested the groans, the sighs, the tears and the prayers of all the Just of the Old Testament, because from me, as from the most fruitful Root of Jesse, sprang my Daughter, the Immaculate Mother, and Jesus Christ, her son and the son of God, source of the new law of love”
  • Pause for silence
  • Reflection on the texts we have heard, helped by the following questions:
    • Mary is the fruit of Anne’s faith in the divine mercy – Do you desire that your life too be enlightened by this spirituality, in order to wait for and obtain such fruits?
    • Poverty and expectation made Anne’s womb fruitful with the “Immaculate Conception”; do you truly want your heart to be like that of the Holy Mother?
    • Mother Rosa felt the presence of St Anne alive in her life: Let us learn from Mother Rosa to love and to make known the Holy Mother:
      • “How many facts I could mention to show you how the Holy Mother, Mother of the great Mother of God, wants to be invoked in our needs and loved as the Mother who brings us to the great Virgin, Most Holy, and to blessed God!”
      • “She loves us, so that in these two hearts of Jesus and Mary you may all be purified, consumed in this most sweet love”

AND WITH THE PATRON SAINTS

  • Introduction (by the Leader or the Sister Facilitator)
  • Reading: Statutes art. 49

  • Substitute reading: Sir 44:1–15
  • Pause for silence for interiorizing the texts we have heard
  • Personal reflection, in the light of the following questions:
    • Call to mind the “illustrious men” of whom the Bible speaks, that is, those who have gone before us in the faith
    • Are you aware that your faith is founded on the faith of these virtuous men, dear to God?
    • Do you feel responsible for the “growth in faith” of your brothers and sisters?
    • In everyday life, do you feel distracted by opportunities, swept along by the models and false values that this society presents to you, or do you let yourself be drawn by the example of the saints?
    • Mother Rosa had a great devotion to the Saints. Can you say to which ones in particular, and why?

      • In the light of her devotion, ask yourself: do I live devotion to the Saints? Is it perhaps still mere devotionalism, or a help for walking more swiftly toward Christ, spurred on by their example and their intercession?
